---
title: "Count endpoints — `[count_model]`"
---

A count endpoint scores a **non-negative integer** observation — seizures per week, lesions
per scan, exacerbations per interval — against a **Poisson** or **negative-binomial** law
whose mean is any expression over the model's parameters. It is the count member of the
non-Gaussian family that [`[binary_model]`](categorical.qmd) belongs to, declared with a
`[count_model]` block, and needs `--features survival` like the binary endpoint (#2877).

## The `[count_model]` block

```ini
[count_model]
cmt        = 4
type       = poisson                                 ; or negbin
log_lambda = log(BASE) + BETA * (WT / 70 - 1) + ETA_C ; log of the mean count per record
; negbin only:
; r        = R                                        ; size (> 0); variance λ + λ²/r
```

Observations for the block's `cmt` carry the count in `DV` (`EVID = 0`). For each record
the model computes the mean `λ` and scores

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Poisson:}\quad -\log P(k) &= \lambda - k\log\lambda + \ln\Gamma(k+1), \\
\text{NegBin:}\quad -\log P(k) &= -\Big[\ln\frac{\Gamma(k+r)}{\Gamma(r)\,\Gamma(k+1)}
  + r\log\frac{r}{r+\lambda} + k\log\frac{\lambda}{r+\lambda}\Big].
\end{aligned}
$$

The constant `ln Γ(k+1)` is kept, so the OFV is the full `−2 log L` — NONMEM's
`F_FLAG = 1` (`-2LL`) objective with `Y = −2·LOG(PMF)`, and R's `-2 * logLik()`.

### Keys

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|-----|----------|---------|
| `cmt` | yes | Data-file `CMT` column value for this endpoint's rows. |
| `type` | no | `poisson` (the default) or `negbin`. |
| `lambda` | one of `lambda` / `log_lambda` | The mean count `λ` of the record. Must evaluate to a finite, positive number. |
| `log_lambda` | one of `lambda` / `log_lambda` | `log λ` instead — any finite number. The natural spelling of a log-linear model, and it cannot go non-positive. |
| `r` | `negbin` only | The size `r > 0`. Variance `λ + λ²/r`; the Poisson is the limit `r → ∞`. |

Every expression reads the same namespace as a `[binary_model]` predictor: θ, η,
covariates (each record's own value, as a `$PRED` reads the current record), values from
`[individual_parameters]`, and `TIME`. A count-only model needs no `[structural_model]`,
`[error_model]` or `[individual_parameters]` block. `r` is an ordinary θ — write
`r = R` with `theta R(5, 0.01, 1000)`, or put a covariate or random effect on it.
A θ level block (`theta PLACEBO[STUDY, TIME](0.0)`) read bare in the mean is scored at
each record's own level, and the count records define the block's levels, as binary
records do (see [θ level blocks](parameters.qmd)).

### Exposure and offsets

Counts over intervals of different length need no dedicated key: put the exposure in the
mean. With the interval length in a data column `DUR`,
`log_lambda = log(RATE) + log(DUR) + ETA_C` (or `lambda = RATE * DUR * exp(ETA_C)`)
is the Poisson rate model with an offset, R's `offset(log(DUR))`.

### Where the law is undefined

A `lambda` that is zero, negative or not finite, a `log_lambda` that is not finite or whose
exponential overflows, and an `r` that is not finite and positive have no count law. At
such a point the subject's objective is the finite `1e20` repellent (as for an overflowed
binary predictor), never a `NaN`, so the optimizer is pushed back rather than stopped; a
simulated record there is skipped with a warning naming the subject and the CMT. Writing
the mean as `log_lambda` removes the positivity edge altogether.

## Negative-binomial parameterisation

ferx uses the **mean / size** form: mean `λ`, size `r`, variance `λ + λ²/r`. The other
common spellings map onto it as follows.

| Tool | Spelling | In ferx |
|------|----------|---------|
| R `dnbinom(k, size, mu)`, `MASS::glm.nb` (`theta`), `lme4::glmer.nb` | size, mean | `r = size`, `lambda = mu` |
| nlmixr2 `dnbinomMu(size, mu)` | size, mean | `r = size`, `lambda = mu` |
| Dispersion `α` (Stata `nbreg`, many papers; `var = μ + αμ²`) | `α = 1/r` | `r = 1 / ALPHA` |
| NONMEM | user-coded `$PRED` log-PMF (`GAMLN`), any form | the size form as coded in `nonmem_anchor/count_nb_laplace.ctl` |
| Monolix (`count` observation model) | user-coded `pCount` | write its `log(P)` in the size form above |

## Data format

`DV` holds the count. A DV on a count CMT that is not a finite non-negative integer
(`2.5`, `-1`, `inf`) stops the read with a message naming the subject, the CMT and the
time; a missing DV (`.`) is an `MDV = 1` row, as on every endpoint.

```csv
ID,TIME,DV,CMT,EVID,MDV,WT,TRT
1,0,6,1,0,0,73.2,0
1,7,9,1,0,0,73.2,0
1,21,3,1,0,0,73.2,1
```

## Estimation

| Method | Count | Notes |
|--------|:-----:|-------|
| **FOCEI** / **Laplace** | ✓ | Default. The data term is non-Gaussian, so FOCEI on a count row *is* the Laplace marginal; FOCE gives the same objective here. The inner gradient, the exact η-Hessian of the `½ log\|H\|` term and the outer gradient come from the subject's compiled plan, as for [binary](../estimation/categorical.qmd#analytic-inner-gradient). |
| **SAEM** | ✓ | No Laplace approximation; preferred for very sparse counts. |
| **IMP** | ✓ | Importance-sampling marginal likelihood. |
| Gauss–Newton (`gn`, `gn_hybrid`) | — | Refused (`E_COUNT_GN_UNSUPPORTED`): its Hessian is Gaussian-specific. |

On the validation fixtures below, IMP lands on the Laplace optimum (1514.514 Poisson,
1697.356 NB, against 1514.514 / 1697.356), and SAEM within 0.5 and 2.6 OFV of it at the
default settings — its stochastic approximation, as on a binary endpoint.

A count mean or size that the expression compiler cannot represent exactly keeps the
finite-difference inner gradient, and the "*N* of *M* subjects use finite-difference
inner gradients" warning says so.

## Validation

`tests/count_nonmem_anchor.rs` holds the fixtures `nonmem_anchor/count_pois.*` and
`count_nb.*` (60 subjects × 6 records; the mean reads `WT`, which varies between subjects,
and `TRT`, which changes within each subject):

| Case | ferx OFV | NONMEM (`LAPLACE -2LL`) | R |
|------|---------:|------------------------:|--:|
| Poisson, fixed effects | 1775.3799168106 | 1775.3799168107 | `glm`: 1775.3799165101 ¹ |
| NegBin, fixed effects | 1739.1620527867 | 1739.1620527867 | `glm.nb`: 1739.1620527867 |
| Poisson, random intercept | 1514.5136400073 | 1514.5136399861 | `glmer`: 1514.51389 ² |
| NegBin, random intercept | 1697.3555547131 | 1697.3555547199 | `glmer.nb`: see ³ |

¹ At R's own (more precise) optimum, where ferx gives 1775.3799165101 as well.
² At glmer's optimum ferx and NONMEM agree to 3.6e-9; glmer's reported deviance is 2.5e-4
higher, from its own inner solve. ³ At glmer.nb's optimum ferx and NONMEM agree to 3.3e-9
(1697.44362), while glmer.nb reports −2 log L = 1697.2560; its outer `r` loop ended with
"iteration limit reached", and that figure is not the Laplace objective.

Every row is evaluated under Laplace, FOCEI and FOCE at NONMEM's estimates (ferx's
objective is within 2.1e-8 of NONMEM's on all of them), on the exact derivatives; the
Tier-3 test fits both random-intercept models to convergence from the file's initial
estimates and lands on NONMEM's optimum.

## Simulation and prediction

`simulate()` and `--simulate` draw one count per count record — a Poisson draw, or the
negative binomial as its gamma–Poisson mixture — on the shared seeded stream, with `ipred`
carrying the record's mean `λ`. Like a binary endpoint a count is observed on the fixed
grid, so a `[simulation]` block needs `times`.

`predict_categorical()` returns `Prediction::Rate { lambda, size }` for a count record
(`size` is `None` for a Poisson endpoint); `Prediction::prob(k)` turns it into `P(Y = k)`.

## Diagnostics (sdtab)

A count endpoint contributes one sdtab row per record: `DV` the count, `PRED` the mean at
`η = 0`, `IPRED` the mean at the subject's EBE, and `IWRES` the Pearson residual
`(k − λ)/√Var` (`Var = λ`, or `λ + λ²/r`). `CWRES` is blank, as for a binary record. The
rows round-trip through `.fitrx` with the binary ones.
